It is materially different from the measured-dead single-dose variants.

It can regularize, but its measured improvement over no auxiliary task was only 0.0001 and it is already part of the known-best stack rather than the strongest next intervention.

The aggressive compound regularization package already failed badly at 0.5954, so reducing embeddings from k=16 to k=8 is the strongest clean, untried overfit intervention. It directly limits sparse-ID memorization, has low cost, and retains a plausible gain of up to 0.003 with 13 iterations remaining.

rejected.reason: The journal already tested the coherent aggressive package and it regressed primary from 0.6018 to 0.5954; repeating it would ignore measured evidence.
The curve has only a narrow near-peak checkpoint region and then declines, so averaging offers mainly a smaller 0.000-0.003 variance benefit rather than addressing excess capacity directly.
Its measured three-seed improvement was only 0.0001 and it is already part of the known-best stack elsewhere, making it less promising than the untried capacity reduction.

method_selection.citation: SWA (Izmailov et al.); EMA training practice; `research/models-losses-hparams.md` seed-variance guidance
method_selection.why: Validation peaks around epochs 6-8 and then declines while training loss continues downward, indicating mild overfit. Several near-peak checkpoints are available, satisfying the averaging precondition. SWA/EMA is the strongest untried overfit treatment after the aggressive regularization package and k=8 capacity reduction both underperformed, with an honest expected gain of 0.000-0.003 mainly from variance reduction.

rejected.reason: The journal already tested the prescribed aggressive compound package and it fell to 0.5954, far below the 0.6018 baseline; repeating it is not justified.
The k=8 test scored 0.6009 and failed to improve the baseline, so capacity reduction has already produced negative evidence.
Although it can regularize, measured benefit was only 0.0001 in the library and it is already running elsewhere; SWA/EMA better matches the available cluster of near-peak checkpoints.
